{{Short description|German mathematician and politician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=August 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=August 2021}}
'''Roswitha Blind''' (also published as '''Roswitha Hammer'''){{r|msn|mg}} is a German mathematician, specializing in [[convex geometry]], [[discrete geometry]], and [[polyhedral combinatorics]], and a politician and organizer for the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany]] in [[Stuttgart]].

==Mathematics==
As Roswitha Hammer, Blind completed a Ph.D. in 1974 at the [[University of Stuttgart]]. Her dissertation, ''Über konvexe Strukturen und die Beziehungen zur elementaren Konvexität'', concerned [[convex geometry]] and [[discrete geometry]] and was supervised by [[Kurt Leichtweiss]].{{r|mg}}

She is best known in mathematics for a 1987 publication with Peter Mani-Levitska in which, solving a conjecture of [[Micha Perles]], she and Mani-Levitska proved that the combinatorial structure of [[simple polytope]]s is completely determined by their graphs.{{r|bm}} This result has been called the Blind–Mani theorem{{r|kalai}} or the Perles–Blind–Mani theorem.{{r|gruber}}

In a 1979 publication,{{r|blind}} she introduced a class of [[convex polytope]]s sometimes called the [[Blind polytope]]s, generalizing the [[semiregular polytope]]s and [[Johnson solid]]s, in which all faces are [[regular polytope]]s.{{r|jbc}}

==Politics==
Blind became a city councillor in the Möhringen-Vaihingen district of [[Stuttgart]] in 2004,{{r|family}} stepping down from that seat in 2009 in order to become chair of the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany]] local council group.{{r|dank}} As councillor, in order to better serve the youth of her district, she became chair of a local football club, 1. FC Lauchhau-Lauchäcker, in 2006, also serving as president of the Stuttgart Sports Forum.{{r|fcll}}

She retired from politics in 2014,{{r|family}} and from her position with the football club in 2016.{{r|fcll}}
